title: [Draft] Lemma G of #484: clean proof and Lean 4 formalisation of its core
body:
> ⚠️ **Draft:** the heavy verification (full fresh-copy replays, CI) is still running. Build on this at your own risk.


This PR gives Lemma G (entrance gauge: target-side compensation at nonzero frames, labelled targets, chain scatter) a clean,
self-contained proof and formalises its abstract core in Lean 4.

Lemma G is worth +1.80% of complex `b` under no-bank hosting:

| word | complex `b` |
| --- | --- |
| Lemma-G-free path (kernel79 only, #500) | 1.310216e-3 |
| full gauge/kernel word (#496/#500) | 1.333854e-3 |

#484 is not modified. This branch is stacked on #484's head and adds only `research/e8-lemma-g-lean/`.

### What is proved (Lean 4.21.0 + Mathlib v4.21.0, the pin of `formal/lean` on main)

```lean
theorem LemmaG.Stream.conj_matrix (T : Λ → M ≃ₗ[K] M) (rec : Λ → Λ → M → M) (es : List (Event ι Λ K))
    (l : ι → Λ) (h : ι → M) (hrec : RecipesExact T rec es) (hw : WellLabelled es l) (r : ι) :
    physRun rec es h r = T (labRun es l r) (∑ s, S es r s • (T (l s)).symm (h s))
```

The theorem holds for every semiring `K`, every `K`-module `M` and every family of linear automorphisms `T`. Take any stream of relabel/add/scale/copy/clear events that is well labelled and whose relabels execute `T_B T_A⁻¹`. Then for every input it computes

`h_r ↦ T_{λ¹_r}(Σ_s S_rs T_{λ⁰_s}⁻¹ h_s)`,

where the non-private columns of `S` are exactly what #484's rational scalar replay computes (`S_rowform`; the replay starts the private copies empty, and their columns drop out on inputs with empty private registers).

The other Lean results:
* **Row lemmas** (`row_unit`, `row_pair`). A unit row gives the block `T_{λ¹}T_{λ⁰}⁻¹`; for an entering helper this is the virtual entrance with its wrappers. A paired row gives `T_{λ¹_r}(T_{λ⁰_r}⁻¹h_r + a·T_{λ⁰_s}⁻¹h_s)`.
* **Schedule** (`emit_spec`, `comp_segment`, `centre_forward`, `centre_backward`), proved for an abstract order with strictly monotone rank and instantiated for the subspaces of F₂⁹.
  * The compensation segment and the centre phase are well labelled as soon as the partners stay at their frames.
  * Under (b) and (c), every move is a strict nested ascent (or descent).
  * Each target ends at `L_t = max ℰ_t`.
* **Accounting** (`paid_telescopes`). Paid ranks telescope to `rk λ¹ − rk λ⁰` per register.
* **Bit-side entrance identities** (`Dbit_one_mul`, `Dbit_conj`). `D_I D_P = D_{I−P}`, and conjugation by `diag(g,g)` for `gᵀg = 1`, for every `P`.

All theorems are general: there is no instance enumeration and no `decide`/`native_decide`. Lean proves the abstract core. The schedule lemmas are an a-priori route that is not instantiated on the emitted stream; the stream itself is checked in Python (below). Combining the Lean core with those checks gives that the data rows are W's and the mass identity `mass(W) − Σ_j dim E_j`. `#print axioms` reports only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. `verify.py` builds the package, scans for `sorry`/`axiom`/`native_decide`, and checks every axiom report.

### What stays checked in Python

The instance hypotheses on the emitted streams:

| hypothesis | check | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| well-labelledness | #484 G0/G2/G3, plus the new `code/check_extended_labels.py` | 0 violations on all four words, both orientations; 3 adapter mutants rejected on every word, 2 wrapper mutants on the wrapper words |
| exact transition recipes; the adapter/wrapper bridge | #484 I-tr on all 512 columns (recipes are linear circuits); one non-identity adapter per source and per target, all others identities (`check_extended_labels.py`) | 2945/2945 |
| the scalar identity `S` | #484 replay, all 800 columns | exact |
| endpoint labels | #484 G4 | 0 violations |
| accounting | #484 G2/G3/ACC | 0 violations |
| #433's data-adapter identities | the new `code/check_adapters.py`, every port, all 512 columns, exact | 0 failures on all four words |

Why the extended-label check: #484 §2.1 left adapters and wrappers outside Lemma C as endpoint operators. Register-wise that is right. Each non-identity adapter and each wrapper is the first or last event on its register, and the adapters that sit mid-stream (headline forward: 550 entry, 672 exit) are all identities. So #484's description was imprecise but harmless. Lemma C as stated still needed an unwritten commutation step. The clean proof reads adapters and wrappers as relabel events of an extended label set (tag × frame), so the theorem covers the complete emitted stream, and the condition is checked directly.

With these hypotheses checked exhaustively, and Lemma A (#484 I-helper, exhaustive), the end-to-end identity holds **for every input with empty private registers**. #484's `lg_e2e.py` tested it on 814 sampled columns.

`PROOF.md` §5 lists the other clarifications:
* the relabel-source condition;
* the inherited facts behind "every input" (#433's adapter identities, Lemma A);
* the minimal label condition;
* (a)–(d) are accounting-only;
* explicit side conditions;
* the kernel updates as an instance of the same emitter.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 research/e8-lemma-g-lean/verify.py                                   # Lean only: cache get + build + axioms
python3 research/e8-lemma-g-lean/verify.py --instances /abs/out/of/484/verify # plus the instance checks (numpy)
```
